proposal.explanation: The failure shows bus_active not asserting when expected. The top-ranked patch adds bus_active qualification to the command acceptance condition, directly controlling when the master initiates bus activity. The rhs_substitution patches then propagate the bus_active signal through the physical layer logic (sda_o_next, bus_control_reg, phy_stop_bit, etc.), ensuring consistent bus_active assertion throughout the transaction. This combination addresses the root cause by gating command acceptance on bus_active and then correctly threading that signal through the I2C physical layer state machine.

proposal.explanation: Ranking prioritizes candidates that directly manipulate core I2C physical-layer signals (phy_tx_data, phy_write_bit, phy_read_bit, scl_o, sda_o, missed_ack_reg) and bus activity indicators (bus_active). Substitutions tied to SCL/SDA timing (patch_b42f68f8b120, patch_1eaa912ddb03) and command/read-data handshakes (patch_a614de3b9c24, patch_40a550fb3580, patch_353450f10494) are ranked highest because bus_active failures at cycles 8-17 suggest the bus-active handshake (repeated start, SCL toggling, SDA release) is not completing. Lower-ranked candidates substitute outputs with loosely related status signals (busy, missed_ack_next) that are less likely to restore the precise SCL/SDA sequencing required for bus_active assertion.

ranking.mechanism: phy_tx_data in WRITE_BIT path now driven by scl_o, linking physical bit emission to SCL output state rather than a constant.
phy_write_bit now driven by s_axis_cmd_ready, coupling physical write emission to command interface readiness.
phy_read_bit gated by m_axis_data_tready, so a read operation only proceeds when the output channel can accept data.
phy_read_bit driven by m_axis_data_tvalid_reg, making physical read dependent on valid output register state.
phy_tx_data sourced from missed_ack_next in PHY_STATE_WRITE_BIT_2 path, feeding back ACK status into transmit data.
phy_tx_data sourced from s_axis_data_tready_reg, linking transmit data to data-channel readiness register.
missed_ack_reg updated from scl_negedge, capturing ACK detection on SCL falling edge.
sda_o_next replaced with missed_ack_next, driving SDA output with missed-ACK status.

proposal.explanation: Ranking prioritizes edits that directly target the failing bus_active register (patch_b426c357ff1e, patch_58d634fc40e4) or modify signals feeding bus control sequencing (patch_64d2bd7aca6b, patch_1eaa912ddb03, patch_047dea8ef5d8, patch_c1bf34953ab3, patch_dd3edbcc7820, patch_4d9541c17aad). All are rhs_substitution of same-width signals at lines implicated by dependency analysis. No RTL, test results, or confidence probabilities are included.

ranking.mechanism: Alters phy_tx_data constant 1'b1 to missed_ack_next in PHY_STATE_WRITE_BIT_3; changes data driven onto SDA during write bit phase, potentially affecting bus control timing and downstream bus_active generation.
Replaces missed_ack_reg default 1'b0 with scl_negedge; couples missed ACK detection to SCL falling edge which may shift bus control sequencing and influence bus_active assertion cycles.
Directly substitutes bus_active_reg initialization from 1'b0 to s_axis_cmd_start; since bus_active is the failing port, this edit targets the exact register driving the mismatched output.
Sets bus_active_reg default from 1'b0 to mode_write_multiple_reg; mode_write_multiple_reg reflects multi-byte write intent and may cause earlier bus_active assertion aligned with expected trace.
Changes phy_tx_data from constant 1'b1 to delay_sda_next in PHY_STATE_START_1; modifies SDA data during repeated start sequence, potentially altering bus arbitration timing that feeds bus_active.
Replaces delay_scl_next constant 1'b1 with scl_t in PHY_STATE_WRITE_BIT_2; ties SCL delay release to output enable, which could shift phy_state progression and bus_active timing.
Substitutes sda_o_next constant 1'b1 with missed_ack_next in PHY_STATE_STOP_2; modifies SDA release during stop, possibly affecting bus handover and bus_active deassertion alignment.
Replaces phy_stop_bit constant 1'b0 with scl_t; ties stop condition to SCL output enable, which may cause premature or delayed stop sequencing impacting bus_active.

proposal.explanation: The simulation shows bus_active never reaching 1. The root cause is that bus_active_reg only sets on start_bit, but start_bit never fires because the physical-layer sequencer is stalled: phy_read_bit and phy_tx_data are constants, sda_o_next never releases the bus, and busy_reg never reflects activity. Patches that wire bus_active_reg to the user start command, make phy_read_bit sample SDA, let phy_tx_data follow the transmit window, drive busy_reg from transaction-end or SCL, and release SDA with the missed-ack flag together unblock the physical layer so start_bit can occur and bus_active can assert. The condition gate patch prevents new commands from entering while the bus is busy, avoiding a secondary stall.

ranking.mechanism: bus_active_reg is stuck low because it never sees start_bit; the replacement ties bus_active_reg to s_axis_cmd_start, the user command that actually begins a transaction, so bus_active rises when a new command arrives.

phy_read_bit currently held low; driving it with sda_i makes the controller sample the bus during read phases so data and ack detection proceed, which eventually allows bus_active to deassert correctly.

phy_tx_data hard-coded to 1 prevents data-phase SDA from toggling; using s_axis_data_tready_reg lets the bit follow the true transmit window so ACK/NACK sampling works and bus_active sequencing completes.
busy_reg stays low; substituting scl_i makes busy follow the clock line so the design reports busy while the physical layer is clocking, matching the trace expectation for bus_active correlation.
busy_reg never asserts; m_axis_data_tlast_next goes high at the end of a read transaction, so busy reflects transaction completion and aligns with bus_active deassertion.
sda_o_next fixed high masks slave ACK; missed_ack_next carries the sampled NACK so the bus release sequence sees the correct level and can transition bus_active.
phy_read_bit constant; m_axis_data_tvalid_reg rises when read data is valid, enabling the read-bit sequence that leads to proper bus_active deassertion.
guard s_axis_cmd_ready with bus_active so new commands wait for the bus to be free, preventing premature state entry that stalls bus_active.
